Since the dark-mode change was deliberately abandoned (explicit team decision, nothing merged) and there's a real rationale worth preserving, close it rather than delete it — that keeps the record of *why* it was dropped instead of erasing it.

Concretely, in the `add-dark-mode-toggle` packet directory, edit the file(s) that carry the placeholder text and add a line like:

```
NUCLEAR-GRADE-CLOSED: Dropped for this quarter — team decision (2026-06 meeting) to defer dark mode until design finalizes the color palette. No code merged. Decided by: team, recorded by benjaminhuffer1@gmail.com.
```

That marker line is what the status tool recognizes as "closed" instead of "scaffold." Leave the placeholder-riddled content as-is otherwise — you're not filling it in, since the change isn't happening.

Leave `refactor-auth-flow` alone — it's in-progress work, not stale, and will resolve to `ok` once your teammate adds the missing file. Don't touch it or its `invalid` tag on their behalf.

After adding the closure line, rerun the status check — you should see `add-dark-mode-toggle` as `closed`, `refactor-auth-flow` still `invalid` (expected, in-progress), and `bump-lodash-version` as `ok`.
